To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the region in RhoA between amino acid residues Asp60 and Asp78 is the minimal sequence required for deamidation/transglutamination by the Escherichia colicytotoxic necrotizing factors.

the switch II region of Rho is the essential substrate recognition site for the Escherichia colicytotoxic necrotizing factors 1 and 2 and the Bordetella dermonecrotic toxins, and that the substrate recognition by the cytotoxic necrotization factors is different from that of the dermonecrotizing toxins.
the region of Rha GTPases essential for substrate recognition of the Escherichia colicytotoxic necrotizing factors is located in the switch II domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the region in RhoA that is involved in substrate recognition by the CNF1 toxin and provides evidence for a novel mechanism of substrate recognition by Rho GTP-ases.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the biological effects of the CNF1 toxin.
the identification of the region of RHO involved in substrate recognition by CNF1 and DNT and with the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of Rho activation by these toxins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNF1 and DNT recognize Rho GTPase proteins in different ways, but the precise nature of these interactions is not yet known.
the switch II region of Rho GTPase is the minimal sequence required for deamidation/transglutamination by the CNF1 toxin.
CNF1 is able to recognize the switch II region of all three small Rho GTPase members, whereas DNT recognizes only Rac.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RhoA and Ras share a conserved region in the switch II domain, which is recognized by CNF1 and that this region is not recognized by DNT.
CNF1 deamidates RhoA in the switch II domain, whereas DNT requires the switch I domain in addition.
the substrate specificity of DNT and CNF1 is determined by the presence of the catalytic domains of Rho GTPase and the transglutaminases, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the region of Rha involved in substrate recognition by the toxin CNF1 is located in switch II.
the substrate recognition by CNF1 and DNT is characterized in part by different structural elements of their target proteins, Rho GTPase and Rac/Cdc42.
CNF1 can recognize and modify a Rho/Ras chimera, which is a novel observation and suggests that the CNF1 substrate recognition is not as strict as that of DNT.
